headline: T-Mobile physically cut cable to expel Chinese hackers from network
summary: Phone giant T-Mobile resorted to scissors to sever a compromised system, expelling Chinese state-backed hackers from its network in 2024.
details: T-Mobile's cybersecurity team identified and expelled Chinese government-backed hackers from its network this year, according to Bloomberg. The hackers, identified as Salt Typhoon, targeted hundreds of telecom and data companies to steal customer data and information on U.S. officials.
The campaign compromised major players like AT&T, Verizon, and Charter. T-Mobile managed to avoid a widespread breach by detecting the intrusion early.

After months of searching for suspicious activity, T-Mobile pinpointed an unusual connection originating from another telecom's router. The company then took drastic measures to isolate the compromised system.

T-Mobile's cybersecurity chief, Jeff Simon, along with three colleagues, drove to a data center and physically cut the cable to the affected system, effectively severing its connection to the outside world and expelling the intruders.
caption:
T-Mobile cybersecurity staff resorted to scissors to expel Chinese hackers from their network in 2024, cutting a compromised cable to sever the intrusion.

T-Mobile's cybersecurity team identified and expelled Chinese government-backed hackers from its network this year, according to Bloomberg. The hackers, identified as Salt Typhoon, targeted hundreds of telecom and data companies to steal customer data and information on U.S. officials.

The campaign compromised major players like AT&T, Verizon, and Charter. T-Mobile managed to avoid a widespread breach by detecting the intrusion early.

After months of searching for suspicious activity, T-Mobile pinpointed an unusual connection originating from another telecom's router. The company then took drastic measures to isolate the compromised system.

T-Mobile's cybersecurity chief, Jeff Simon, along with three colleagues, drove to a data center and physically cut the cable to the affected system, effectively severing its connection to the outside world and expelling the intruders.
